name: mcpfold SEO iterative loop
description: One SEO element improved per iteration. Items too large for a single iteration are recorded here with enough detail to be picked up cold on the next iteration. Update `status` and `iteration` as items land.

items.title: Per-URL sitemap lastmod from content, not the build clock
items.problem: Every URL in every child sitemap carried the same BUILD_DATE. Google discards lastmod entirely when a site stamps all URLs identically on each deploy, so the crawl-scheduling signal was worthless across ~hundreds of pSEO pages.
items.solution: scripts/lastmod.mjs maps each route to the source file(s) that produce it and dates it from the last commit touching them (git log -1 --format=%cs), cached per file, falling back to the build date when git is unavailable. Child sitemaps now carry the newest lastmod they contain.
items.verify: node scripts/lastmod.mjs --self-test; e2e 'sitemap lastmod is per-URL content dating'

items.title: Rasterize per-page OG cards to PNG
items.problem: gen-og.mjs emits dist/og/<route>.svg and gen-seo.mjs wires it into og:image and twitter:image for every route. Facebook, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Slack and Discord all REJECT image/svg+xml for og:image, so every page except the home fallback (/og.png) currently renders a blank social card. The code comment in gen-og.mjs already flags this as a deferred follow-up.
items.solution: Add @resvg/resvg-js (or sharp) as an apps/site devDependency; rasterize renderOgSvg() output to 1200x630 PNG in the gen-seo route loop, write dist/og/<route>.png, and point og:image/twitter:image at the PNG. Keep the SVG alongside for debugging. Embed the Inter font bytes or fall back to a system sans that resvg can resolve inside CI containers (resvg does not inherit browser font fallback). Add og:image:width/height/alt per route, and an e2e assertion that og:image ends in .png and returns content-type image/png.
risks: resvg native binary must resolve on the Cloudflare Pages / CI build image
font availability in the build container

items.title: RSS feed is invalid and undiscoverable
items.problem: feed.xml emits <pubDate>2026-01-05</pubDate> — RSS 2.0 requires RFC-822 dates, so readers and Google's blog discovery reject or mis-sort the items. The channel also lacks <language>, <lastBuildDate>, <atom:link rel="self">, and nothing in <head> advertises the feed (no <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml">), so it is effectively unlinked.
items.solution: New scripts/feed.mjs (pure, self-tested) renders the feed: rfc822() converts frontmatter dates to GMT RFC-822 without day-shifting date-only values, an unparseable date drops the pubDate rather than emitting garbage, and the channel now carries atom:link rel=self, language, lastBuildDate (newest post, not the build clock) and guid isPermaLink. index.html adds <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml> so the feed is discoverable from every prerendered page, not just /blog.
items.verify: node scripts/feed.mjs --self-test; e2e 'feed.xml is valid RSS with RFC-822 dates'

items.title: JSON-LD points at /docs, which is not a route
items.problem: softwareApplication() in src/seo/jsonld.ts sets softwareHelp to `${SITE_URL}/docs`. There is no /docs route in App.tsx and it is not in allRoutes(), so the structured data advertises a 404 on every page that emits the SoftwareApplication node.
items.solution: Added validateJsonLdUrls + internalUrlsIn to scripts/seo-audit.mjs: walks every JSON-LD node a route emits, collects internal absolute URLs (normalizing trailing slash, query and hash, ignoring @context and external sameAs/license links), and fails the build on any that is not in allRoutes(). entry-server.tsx now returns jsonLdNodes alongside the serialized tags so the audit reads structure rather than re-parsing HTML. softwareHelp fixed to /guides.
items.note: CORRECTION (iteration 5): /docs is NOT a 404 — it is a sibling static build (S8.1) deployed alongside dist/, so it is served even though allRoutes() never lists it. softwareHelp restored to /docs and the guard now carries an EXTERNALLY_SERVED allowlist for /docs*. The guard itself remains correct and useful.

items.title: No Organization/WebSite node with sameAs + SearchAction
items.problem: The structured data was a bag of disjoint nodes. Nothing declared who publishes the site, the only sameAs links sat on /about, no node carried an @id, and page-type nodes used bare URL strings for isPartOf — so a crawler landing on a directory entry had no way to tie the page to the mcpfold entity.
items.solution: Stable @id URIs (/#organization, /#website) plus an Organization + WebSite pair emitted on every route from jsonLdForPath. Page-type nodes now reference them through publisher/isPartOf instead of standing alone; the /about-only Organization is gone. auditEntityGraph fails the build unless every route carries exactly one of each with the expected @id and every {'@id': …} reference resolves to a node defined in the same graph. validateJsonLdUrls now allows static-asset URLs so Organization.logo doesn't read as dead.
items.decision: Deliberately no SearchAction/sitelinks searchbox: Google retired that rich result in 2023, so declaring one buys nothing and implies a search surface this site doesn't expose.

items.title: Title/description length guards in the build audit
items.problem: auditMeta checked presence and uniqueness but not length. Measured against the real data: comparison intros ran to 591 chars, feature taglines to 298, use-case taglines to 213, glossary definitions to 195 — all used verbatim as <meta name=description> against a ~155-char SERP budget. Comparison titles hit 71 chars once the ' · mcpfold' suffix was appended to an already-61-char metaTitle.
items.solution: clampDescription() in meta.ts trims to the last whole sentence that fits 155 chars, falling back to a word-boundary cut with an ellipsis when the opening sentence overruns or is too short to fill the snippet (MIN_USEFUL=100). Applied inside meta() so no new page type can skip it; full prose still renders in the page body and JSON-LD. withBrand() appends the brand suffix only when it fits within 60 chars and the title does not already say mcpfold. auditMetaLength() enforces both at build time with a warn tier (>60 title, >155 description) and a fail tier (>70/>180/<50). Verified: every description now lands in 104-154 chars.

items.title: Internal linking: no programmatic related-pages mesh
items.problem: Every deep page type linked only within its own silo: a directory entry (89 of them, the most numerous page type) carried just 3 links — back to /directory and its category tags. No topical path existed between directory, guides, glossary, compare, features and use-cases.
items.solution: src/seo/related.ts derives up to 6 cross-silo links per route from existing data — a directory entry now reaches its category, two siblings, the guide for installing it, the glossary term explaining it, and the token calculator. Siblings rotate deterministically by page id so the mesh spreads rather than pointing every page at the same few. RelatedLinks.tsx renders it once in Layout so no page type can forget it, and it is prerendered (not behind an effect) so crawlers see it without JS. validateRelatedLinks fails the build on a dead target, a self-link, or a whole page type losing its block.
items.verify: node scripts/seo-audit.mjs --self-test; e2e 'deep pages carry a cross-silo related-links block'

items.title: Orphan-page + internal-link-graph build guard
items.problem: Nothing verifies that prerendered routes are actually linked from the site. A route can be in the sitemap and reachable only by direct URL.
items.solution: scripts/link-graph.mjs reads back every dist/**/index.html the prerender wrote, extracts the internal <a href> targets, and audits the resulting graph: a dead link (not a route, not under the sibling docs build, not a static file), an orphan (no OTHER page links to it — self-links don't count), or a page with no internal links at all all fail the build. Wired into gen-seo.mjs after the prerender loop, so it checks what actually shipped rather than the data that produced it.

items.title: Breadcrumb JSON-LD coverage across every deep page type
items.problem: Breadcrumb coverage was uneven and hand-written per page type. Deep pSEO pages started their trail at the hub with no Home crumb while shallow pages included one; the hubs themselves, /install, /pricing, /security, /changelog and the token calculator emitted no trail at all; and a directory entry jumped straight from Directory to the server, skipping the category that actually sits between them.
items.solution: crumbsFor() in jsonld.ts derives the trail from the route in one place: always rooted at Home, with the category level inserted for directory entries, hub labels from one table, and legal/deep page types resolved from their own data. jsonLdForPath() now composes pageNodes() + the derived BreadcrumbList, so every hand-written trail is gone and a new page type inherits a correct one. auditBreadcrumbs() fails the build unless every non-home route emits exactly one list, rooted at Home, with contiguous positions and a last item equal to that page's own canonical (and the home page emits none).

items.title: Canonical/trailing-slash and host normalization at the edge
items.problem: The premise in this item was partly wrong. The site deploys to Cloudflare Pages (.github/workflows/pages.yml), which already 308-normalizes a trailing slash and enforces HTTPS on custom domains — so those needed no rule. What was genuinely missing was www -> apex, which Pages does NOT collapse by default while every canonical tag points at https://mcpfold.com. Separately, nothing verified that the existing legacy redirects still resolve.
items.solution: Added a www -> apex 301 to public/_redirects with a comment recording what Pages handles on its own, so nobody re-adds redundant rules. Added auditRedirects to the build: every rule's internal target must resolve to a route (or /docs, or a static file), no rule may shadow a live route, statuses must be 301/302/308, and duplicate sources fail. Verified the shipped rules pass.
items.deferred: The 'redirect chain is at most one hop' e2e from the original plan needs a real deployed host to assert against; the build guard covers the failure mode that is checkable offline.

items.title: Heading hierarchy audit on prerendered HTML
items.problem: No guard that each prerendered page has exactly one <h1>, that it is non-empty, that it contains the page's focus keyword, and that heading levels do not skip.
items.solution: scripts/headings.mjs audits each page's heading outline, scoped to <main> so the shared header, Related block and footer (an <h2> per group on every page) don't drown the signal. Fails the build on a missing or duplicated <h1>, an empty heading at any level, or a level skip. Reuses the single dist read that the link-graph audit already does (readPrerenderedPages now returns the HTML alongside the hrefs). Found and fixed a real violation: /install went h1 -> h3 -> h2, because the install-channel cards had no section heading above them; added 'Choose an install channel' as the h2.
items.deferred: The h1-contains-focus-keyword check from the original plan was left out — too brittle to fail a build on, and keywordFor() lives in TS that the audit script doesn't import. Revisit as a warning tier if wanted, alongside SEO-15's keyword-coverage report.

items.title: Image SEO: alt text, dimensions, lazy loading, modern formats
items.problem: Alt text turned out to be fine on all four images — the real defect was dimensions. The hero demo.svg is the page's LCP element and declared no width/height, so the browser reserved no box and the layout shifted as it loaded. The brand-asset images had the same gap, and nothing was lazy-loaded or priority-hinted.
items.solution: Hero: width/height matching demo.svg's intrinsic 900x557, height:auto to keep it fluid, plus loading=eager and fetchpriority=high so the LCP image stays off the lazy path. Brand and footer images: intrinsic dimensions, loading=lazy, decoding=async, and a more descriptive alt. auditImages (riding the same dist read as the heading audit, scoped to <main>) fails the build on a missing alt attribute, missing width/height, or an image that is both lazy and fetchpriority=high; it warns on an undeclared empty alt (alt='' plus aria-hidden is accepted as deliberate) and on a below-the-fold image with no loading hint.
items.deferred: AVIF/WebP conversion was not done: the only raster image in page content is logo-mark.png at 24-28px, where format conversion saves nothing measurable. The hero is already an SVG. Revisit if photographic content is ever added.

items.title: Core Web Vitals budget enforced in CI
items.problem: Rankings are gated on field CWV; there is currently no LCP/CLS/INP budget in CI and no render-blocking-resource check on the prerendered pages.
items.solution: Add Lighthouse CI (or a Playwright + web-vitals harness) against `vite preview` of dist/ with per-route budgets, run on PRs, failing on regression. Preload the LCP image/font, inline critical CSS, and defer GSAP where it is not above the fold.

items.title: GEO: llms.txt completeness and per-page AI answerability
items.problem: FAQ units existed on five hand-written pages (/, /install, /directory, /pricing, the calculator). The generated pages — 18 client guides, 7 glossary terms, 89 directory entries — had none, and those are exactly the pages an answer engine reaches for. llms.txt was a hand-maintained link list that had drifted: it never mentioned the guides, glossary, compare, features, use-cases or the token calculator at all, so an assistant reading it never learned those page types existed.
items.solution: faqsForPath now derives FAQ units for guide, glossary and directory-entry pages from real adapter and directory data — config path and key, restart behaviour, secret mechanism — so they are true by construction and a new client or server inherits its FAQ automatically. The secrets question is only emitted for the 'shim' and 'native-input' strategies, where the data pins the mechanism down; an 'inline' client gets no invented claim. llms.txt gained the six missing hub links plus /security, and auditLlmsCoverage fails the build when a page the keyword map targets is unreachable from the map (directly or via its listed hub).
items.deferred: The 'lead-answer paragraph in the first 200 words' page-template pattern from the original plan is content work across every deep template, not a one-iteration change. The FAQ units deliver most of the extractability benefit; revisit the lead-answer pattern as its own item.

items.title: Keyword map → page coverage gaps and cannibalization
items.problem: The keyword map still said guide/glossary/compare rows 'get added when those routes land' — they landed long ago. 20 rows covered 10 pages, leaving the guides, glossary, features, use-cases and category collection pages entirely unmeasured. And validateKeywordPages only proved each mapped page exists; nothing detected the same query claimed by two pages.
items.solution: Added 29 rows covering the shipped page types (7 client guides + the hub, 7 glossary terms + the hub, 4 features, 3 personas, 7 category collections) — 49 rows over 40 pages. auditKeywordMap fails the build when one query (case- and whitespace-normalized) is claimed by two pages, and warns when a generated page type has nothing tracked against it at all. Recorded the deliberate three-way split of the 'mcp config manager' cluster in the map: / owns the commercial head term, /glossary/mcp-config-manager the definitional phrasing, /compare/mcp-config-manager the comparison phrasing.
items.note: Volumes are order-of-magnitude planning estimates, consistent with the existing rows' convention — they are not measured data and should be replaced from a real keyword tool before driving decisions.
